## The Agent Judge 0.17.0 train

AgentWorks BOM 1.21.0 is the supported way to consume **Agent Judge 0.17.0** — the release in which a
requirements judge stops passing a specification it never checked, and `NOT_APPLICABLE` becomes its own
judgment status. 0.17.0 is a breaking result-format change for Java consumers, so this BOM moves every
member that compiles against the judge in the same step.

It also converges the portfolio on **one Claude Agent SDK version**, `claude-code-sdk` 1.7.0.

### What moves

| Member | 1.20.0 | 1.21.0 | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `agent-judge` (10 modules) | 0.15.2 | **0.17.0** | EARS and RFC 2119 judges reject an empty roster; five judgment statuses; intended compile break on exhaustive switches over `JudgmentStatus` |
| `agent-workflow` (8 modules) | 0.12.2 | **0.12.3** | `JudgeGate` and `TieredGate` route a `NOT_APPLICABLE` aggregate as **inconclusive** — not a pass, not an escalation |
| `agent-bench` (2 modules) | 0.6.2 | **0.6.3** | scores benchmark runs through juries; recompiled against 0.17.0 |
| `agent-experiment` (3 modules) | 0.8.0 | **0.9.0** | verdict interpretation against Judge 0.17.0 and Workflow 0.12.3 |
| `claude-code-sdk` | 1.6.0 | **1.7.0** | destroys the Claude CLI process tree before closing its streams, so a cancelled run no longer leaves the CLI alive |
| `agent-client` (28 modules) | 0.30.0 | **0.31.0** | interrupt tracking in the Claude model, on SDK 1.7.0 |
| `agent-journal` (6 modules) | 1.10.0 | **1.10.1** | capture adapters re-pinned to SDK 1.7.0 and `gemini-cli-sdk` 0.30.0 |
| `agent-hooks` (4 modules) | 0.8.2 | **0.8.3** | re-pinned to SDK 1.7.0 |

`acp-java-sdk` 0.17.0, `agent-memory` 0.5.1 and `agent-sandbox` 0.10.2 are unchanged.

### Four modules the BOM now manages

`agent-acp`, `agent-junie`, `agent-starter-junie` and `junie-cli-capture` were published by their projects
but were neither managed nor deliberately excluded, so a consumer had to pin them by hand while every
sibling came from the BOM. They are managed from 1.21.0: **85 managed coordinates, up from 81.** Nothing was
removed.

### If you are on 0.16.0 of the judge, this is the upgrade that matters

`EarsJudge.create` and `Rfc2119Judge.create` used to accept an empty roster, and a conjunctive rollup over
an empty denominator is vacuously true — 0.16.0 returns `PASS` for a specification with no requirements in
it, indistinguishable in every stored field from one that was genuinely met. **A stored `PASS` with a
`criteriaTotal` or `constraintsTotal` of `0` identifies an affected run.** 0.17.0 refuses the empty roster
in the judge and again in the rollup.

Because the status set changed, a gate built on 0.15.2 has no branch for the new status. That is why
Workflow, Bench and Experiment move with the judge rather than after it: on 1.21.0 every path to
`agent-judge` resolves 0.17.0, and every gate on that path understands what it receives.

### Upgrading

```xml
<dependencyManagement>
  <dependencies>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>io.github.markpollack</groupId>
      <artifactId>agentworks-bom</artifactId>
      <version>1.21.0</version>
      <type>pom</type>
      <scope>import</scope>
    </dependency>
  </dependencies>
</dependencyManagement>
```

Then declare AgentWorks dependencies without versions. Importing the BOM also overrides the versions
members pin for each other, so a consumer receives the set above even where a member's own POM names an
earlier sibling. Two limits are worth knowing: a version you write on your own direct dependency wins over
the BOM, and if you import another BOM earlier that manages the same coordinate, the first import wins.

Java consumers of the judge should read the 0.17.0 migration guide before upgrading — the result-format
change is deliberate and it will not compile silently.

### Provenance

Every member version this BOM advances was published through the certified consumer-rooted SBOM procedure:
each module's independently resolved consumer closure matched its published CycloneDX SBOM
component-for-component, dependency SCA was green under frozen scanner controls, and post-publication
verification confirmed the artifacts on Maven Central are byte-identical to what was certified.
`bom-verification` passes 9/9 (plain / Boot 3.5 / Boot 4 scenarios, `RequireUpperBoundDeps` and Jackson
convergence) resolving these exact published versions.
